title: Codex CLI rollout line (observed v1)
description: One JSONL line of an OpenAI Codex rollout file (~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<ISO8601>-<uuid>.jsonl, or ~/.codex/archived_sessions/<same-name>.jsonl). Derived empirically from an operator corpus of 966 rollout files / 1,510,157 lines written by codex-cli 0.46.0 through 0.146.0-alpha.3 (2025-10 to 2026-07), plus three controlled `codex exec` captures on 0.137.0 (2026-07-25). Nothing here is invented: every property was observed. Strictness lives in `required`; every object is open (`additionalProperties` defaults to true) because OpenAI owns this format and evolves it continuously. Top-level line types are validated strictly (the set has grown only from 4 to 7 across the whole corpus, so a new one is a signal an importer must see), while `response_item`/`event_msg` payload variants are matched with if/then so unrecognized payload types pass with only `type` required (that set grew from 10 to 34 over the same window). The companion record schema for ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl is $defs/sessionIndexRecord; it is deliberately not a branch of the root oneOf because it lives in a different file.

timestamp.description: UTC ISO-8601 with exactly three fractional digits and a literal Z. 1,510,157 of 1,510,157 lines matched this shape; no other timestamp encoding was observed anywhere in the corpus.

lineEnvelope.description: Every rollout line, in every observed version, is an object with exactly these three keys. No line carried a fourth top-level key.

sessionMetaLine.description: Session header. Always the first line of a rollout file (964/964 non-empty files). May recur later in the same file: Codex Desktop re-emits it on each resume of the thread (up to 556 occurrences in one file), and a forked thread writes its own meta at line 0 followed by the source thread's meta at line 1.

sessionMetaPayload.description: Load-bearing for an importer: `id` is the session identity (it equals the UUID in the rollout filename in 802/802 checked files) and `cwd` is the placement anchor. Everything else is optional-typed; presence varies sharply by version (see notes).

id.description: UUIDv7 thread id. Matches the filename UUID for the first meta of a file.

timestamp.description: Session-start instant. Present on 100% of metas but distinct from the envelope timestamp on 5,047 of 5,050 (the envelope is written slightly later).

cli_version.description: Semver, sometimes with an -alpha.N suffix. 46 distinct values observed, 0.46.0 through 0.146.0-alpha.3.

source.description: String for human-driven sessions ("vscode", "cli", "exec"); object for spawned sub-agent threads. Union is real, not an artifact.

session_id.description: Redundant duplicate of `id` introduced ~2026-04. Never observed to disagree with `id`.

parent_thread_id.description: Present on 591 sub-agent session files. Points at the spawning thread's `id`; that thread's rollout file holds the spawn_agent function_call.

forked_from_id.description: Present when the thread was forked from another. The forked-from thread's own session_meta is replayed as the next line of the same file.

instructions.description: Pre-0.100 name for the system prompt slot; observed only as null on the single 0.46.0 session. Superseded by base_instructions.

agent_nickname.description: Human-readable label given to a spawned agent (e.g. a scientist surname). Cosmetic; not an identifier.

agent_path.description: Slash-delimited position of this agent in the multi-agent tree, e.g. "/root/some_task". Root is "/root".

context_window.description: Observed shape: {"window_id": "<uuid>"}. Correlates with `compacted` lines' window ids.

dynamic_tools.description: Tool/namespace declarations available to the thread. Two observed element shapes: namespace entries {type,name,description,tools} and flat tool entries {name,description,inputSchema[,namespace,deferLoading]}.

sessionSourceObject.description: session_meta.payload.source when the thread is a spawned sub-agent (855 files).

subagent.description: Observed as an object with a `thread_spawn` descriptor (711), or as {"other": "<string>"} (144).

thread_spawn.description: parent_thread_id (711/711) is the spawning thread's id and is the child->parent linkage. agent_path and agent_role are frequently null (675 and 82 of 711 respectively).

instructionsBlob.description: Observed shape is exactly {"text": "<system prompt>"} on all 5,049 occurrences.

gitInfo.description: Repo context at session start, present on 4,379 metas. Keys observed: branch (4309), commit_hash (4088), repository_url (4088). All three are individually optional.

responseItemLine.description: A model-conversation item: the authoritative content stream. These are the records Codex replays to the model on resume; the parallel event_msg stream is UI-derived. 773,449 lines.

responseItemPayload.description: Discriminated by `type`. Observed values, by frequency: function_call, function_call_output, reasoning, message, custom_tool_call_output, custom_tool_call, web_search_call, agent_message, tool_search_call, tool_search_output. `compaction` also occurs, but only nested inside a `compacted` line's replacement_history. Unlisted types validate against the base constraint alone.

itemProvenance.description: Fields that decorate most response_item payloads without carrying conversation content. `id` is the provider's item id (prefix encodes the kind: msg_, rs_, fc_, fco_, ctc_, ctco_, ws_, tsc_, tso_, amsg_) and is NOT the tool-call linkage key. Turn attribution lives under internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough (current) or metadata (2026-02..2026-04); both observed only as {"turn_id": "<uuid>"}.

messagePayload.description: A conversation message. 107,526 observed. `content` was an array on 100% of them (never a bare string), and every element was an object.

role.description: Observed: "assistant" (72,907), "user" (29,094), "developer" (5,525). "system" was never observed. Not enumerated so a future role does not fail validation.

phase.description: Observed: "commentary" (55,504), "final_answer" (17,391). Introduced ~2026-05; absent on older assistant messages.

contentBlock.description: Observed block types: input_text (106,007), output_text (72,907), input_image (466). input_text/output_text carry `text`; input_image carries `image_url` (a data: URI in every observed case) and optionally `detail`.

reasoningPayload.description: Model reasoning. 148,195 observed; `encrypted_content` was a non-null string on 100% of them and `summary` was an array on 100% (empty on 131,928 -- i.e. 89% of reasoning items carry no plaintext at all). `content` was present-and-null on 71% and never non-null. The encrypted blob is opaque and account-scoped: it is evidence to preserve, not text to render.

summaryBlock.description: Only one shape was ever observed: {"type": "summary_text", "text": "..."} (30,110 blocks).

functionCallPayload.description: A model tool call. LINKAGE KEY IS `call_id`, not `id`: call_id was present on 100% of 209,662 function_calls (always prefixed "call_"), while `id` (prefix "fc_") appeared on only 11.3% and is the provider item id. `arguments` was a JSON-encoded string on 100% -- never a nested object. Observed names include exec_command, write_stdin, wait, update_plan, view_image, shell, spawn_agent/wait_agent/close_agent/send_input/send_message/list_agents/resume_agent (multi-agent), and mcp__<server>__<tool>.

functionCallOutputPayload.description: Result of a function_call, linked solely by `call_id`. Across 257,456 output records (function/custom/tool_search) the referenced call_id always appeared earlier in the same file; no output ever preceded its call.

customToolCallPayload.description: A freeform (non-JSON-argument) tool call. `input` is raw text, not JSON. Only two names observed: apply_patch (24,073) and exec (23,642). `status` was "completed" on 100% of 47,715.

toolOutput.description: Tool output is a bare string (232,885 observed) or an array of content blocks (24,457). Both encodings appear in the same versions and even the same session; an importer must handle the union. No other encoding was observed.

webSearchCallPayload.description: A hosted web-search tool call. Deliberately requires nothing beyond `type`: 1,906 of 2,366 carried NO id field at all, and none carried `call_id`. When `id` is present (460, prefix "ws_") it is what the paired event_msg/web_search_end references in its own `call_id` field -- the only place in the format where an event_msg `call_id` points at a response_item `id`.

toolSearchCallPayload.description: Client-side deferred-tool lookup. Note `arguments` here is an OBJECT ({query, limit}), unlike function_call where it is a JSON string.

toolSearchOutputPayload.description: Result of a tool_search_call. Carries `tools`, not `output`.

interAgentMessagePayload.description: A message routed between agents in a multi-agent thread tree (response_item type "agent_message" -- not to be confused with the UI event of the same name). `author` and `recipient` are agent paths such as "/root" and "/root/<task>"; both were present on 100% of 413 observations, as was an id with prefix "amsg_". Content blocks are input_text and/or encrypted_content. Always accompanied by an adjacent inter_agent_communication_metadata line.

eventMsgLine.description: A UI/telemetry event. Largely a re-rendering of the response_item stream for the transcript view, plus information that exists nowhere else (token accounting, exec/patch results, turn lifecycle, multi-agent activity). 701,177 lines. See notes for which are authoritative and which are skippable noise.

eventMsgPayload.description: Discriminated by `type`; 24 values observed: token_count, agent_message, agent_reasoning, patch_apply_end, user_message, task_started, task_complete, exec_command_end, web_search_end, mcp_tool_call_end, context_compacted, thread_settings_applied, sub_agent_activity, turn_aborted, collab_agent_spawn_end, thread_name_updated, collab_waiting_end, view_image_tool_call, collab_close_end, item_completed, thread_goal_updated, thread_rolled_back, collab_agent_interaction_end, collab_resume_end. Only the variants an importer plausibly reads are constrained below; the rest validate on `type` alone.

eventUserMessage.description: Emitted for operator input. Nothing in the response_item stream distinguishes a real operator turn from a synthetic user-role message (environment_context, AGENTS.md injection, subagent_notification, turn_aborted notices) -- both are message/role=user -- so this event is the primary discriminator, though not an exact one (96% precision / 86% recall against a tag-prefix heuristic; see notes 3.7). 18,507 observed.

images.description: Inline data: URIs of pasted images.

local_images.description: Absolute paths to the same images on disk; the files are outside the rollout and may be gone.

eventAgentMessage.description: UI mirror of assistant output. Does NOT pair 1:1 with message/role=assistant response_items (126,347 events vs 72,907 items): a single assistant response is emitted as several phase-tagged events.

eventAgentReasoning.description: Plaintext reasoning summary for the UI. Where a response_item/reasoning has an empty `summary`, this event is the only human-readable trace of that reasoning.

eventTokenCount.description: Usage and rate-limit snapshot; 366,554 lines, 24% of the entire corpus. Both fields are nullable. This is the only place token usage is recorded.

eventTaskStarted.description: Opens a turn. `turn_id` was present on 100% of 17,311 and is the join key for turn_context and the *_metadata_passthrough turn ids on response items.

eventTaskComplete.description: Closes a turn normally. `last_agent_message` is null when the turn produced no assistant text (observed on API-error turns, where the error itself is never persisted to the rollout).

eventTurnAborted.description: Closes a turn abnormally (269 observed). An importer must treat any tool call still open at this point as terminated-without-result.

eventExecCommandEnd.description: Full result of a shell execution, keyed by the originating function_call's `call_id` (resolved to a same-file response_item call on 12,236/12,236). Carries exit_code, stdout/stderr and a parsed command classification that the response_item output string does not.

parsed_cmd.description: Classifier output; observed element types read {cmd,name,path}, search {cmd,path,query}, list_files {cmd,path}, unknown {cmd}.

eventPatchApplyEnd.description: Result of an apply_patch custom_tool_call. `changes` is a map from absolute file path to a change descriptor; observed descriptor types are update {unified_diff, move_path}, add {content}, delete {content}. 17,507 of 29,399 did NOT resolve to a call_id present in the same file's response_item stream (the calls had been replaced by compaction) -- so this event is often the only surviving record of an edit.

eventMcpToolCallEnd.description: MCP tool result. `result` is a tagged union with exactly one of Ok (an MCP CallToolResult) or Err (a string message).

eventWebSearchEnd.description: Search results. `call_id` here references a response_item/web_search_call's `id` (prefix "ws_"), not a call_id; when the search call carried no id the reference dangles by construction (4,048 of 4,508).

results.description: Observed element type: text_result {ref_id, title, url, domain, snippet, thumbnail_url} with everything but ref_id/type optional.

eventSubAgentActivity.description: Child-thread lifecycle as seen from the parent (2,189 observed, all 2026-07). `agent_thread_id` is the child session's `id` -- i.e. the UUID of the child's own rollout file -- and `event_id` is the parent's spawn/interaction call_id.

eventCollabAgentSpawnEnd.description: Older (2026-04) multi-agent spawn record. `new_thread_id` is the child session id and is nullable while status is pending_init.

eventThreadNameUpdated.description: The generated thread title; this is the value mirrored into ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl.

eventThreadRolledBack.description: The operator rewound the thread by `num_turns`. The rolled-back lines remain in the file; nothing is deleted. An importer that replays file order without honoring this will resurrect abandoned turns.

turnContextLine.description: Execution settings in force for a turn, written next to the operator input. 25,472 lines against 17,311 task_started events, so not strictly one per turn -- a settings change mid-session emits another.

turnContextPayload.description: Note there is no `type` field inside this payload. `turn_id` is required by nothing: it was absent on the 0.46.0 session (185 lines) and present on every line after. cwd/model/approval_policy/sandbox_policy/effort/summary were present on 100% of observations.

sandbox_policy.description: Discriminator renamed: 0.46.0 used `mode`, every later version uses `type`. Values observed: workspace-write (23,087), read-only (2,385).

user_instructions.description: Project AGENTS.md content, inlined. Present on turn_context in 2026-02/03; later versions inject it as a synthetic user-role message instead.

compactedLine.description: History compaction. The line records the REPLACEMENT history that the model sees from this point on; the pre-compaction response_items remain earlier in the same file. 2,470 lines. An importer that concatenates the file's response_items and then also expands replacement_history will double-count.

compactedPayload.description: No `type` field inside the payload. `window_id` is an integer in older versions and a UUID string in newer ones -- a real union, not a survey artifact.

replacement_history.description: Bare response_item payloads (no envelope). 409,186 were type=message; 2,470 were type=compaction, a payload type that never appears as a standalone response_item line.

worldStateLine.description: Snapshot of ambient context the client injects (environments, AGENTS.md digest, skills/plugins/apps instruction toggles, permissions hash). Client bookkeeping; carries no conversation content. 2,126 lines, first seen 2026-02.

interAgentCommunicationMetadataLine.description: Marker written adjacent to a response_item/agent_message saying whether the delivery triggers a turn in the recipient. 413 lines, all 2026-07, 1:1 with response_item/agent_message.

sessionIndexRecord.description: One line of ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl -- a separate file, not a rollout line, hence not a branch of the root oneOf. Append-only and lossy: 700 records covering 681 distinct ids, of which 525 had a live rollout file and 156 did not; 279 rollout files had no index entry at all (notably every `codex exec` run). It is a title cache for the Desktop/TUI picker, NOT an authoritative session inventory. `id` joins to session_meta.payload.id.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. "2026-07-24T00:31:37.883386Z". Unlike rollout envelope timestamps (3 fractional digits) this field carries 6, so a single timestamp regex cannot cover both files.
